message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering the 24-hour window ending 2026-07-05 05:10 IST (2026-07-04 23:40 UTC). One confirmed new relevant product finding was retained: Microsoft Edge. One Linux kernel item is listed as a possible Ubuntu-related match needing review because the fresh source is NVD/kernel.org, but I did not find an Ubuntu-specific advisory tying it to Ubuntu packages in this window.

**Finding 1**

- Product: Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based), including Edge Stable and related Edge entries where applicable
- Issue: Microsoft Edge security update with newly published Edge CVE entries on July 3, 2026. Public CVE feeds list a broad Edge batch, including CVE-2026-56645, CVE-2026-57975, CVE-2026-57981, CVE-2026-57984, CVE-2026-57985, CVE-2026-57986, CVE-2026-57988, CVE-2026-57991, CVE-2026-57992, CVE-2026-57993, CVE-2026-58276, CVE-2026-58278, CVE-2026-58282 through CVE-2026-58299, CVE-2026-58300, and CVE-2026-58522 through CVE-2026-58524.
- Severity: Mixed. Tenable/NVD-mirrored entries list CVE-2026-56645 as Critical, CVE-2026-57991 as High, and CVE-2026-58282 as Medium; other entries in the batch vary.
- Description: Microsoft Edge Stable 150.0.4078.48 was released on July 2, with the Microsoft release notes pointing to stable-channel security updates. July 3 CVE entries describe several Edge vulnerability classes, including heap buffer overflow, use-after-free, type confusion, improper authorization, improper input validation, SSRF/spoofing, path traversal or link-following, information disclosure, and Edge for Android issues.
- Why it appears relevant: Microsoft Edge is explicitly listed in Products.txt, and the fresh CVE entries name Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) or Microsoft Edge for Android directly.
- Sources: Microsoft Edge Stable release notes (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnote-stable-channel), Microsoft Edge security release notes (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnotes-security), Tenable CVE-2026-56645 (https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-56645), Tenable CVE-2026-57991 (https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-57991), Stack.watch Microsoft vulnerability listing (https://stack.watch/product/microsoft/), and Microsoft Security Update Guide (https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/).

**Possible Matches Needing Review**

- Product: Ubuntu / Linux kernel
- Issue: CVE-2026-53362
- Severity: Not clearly stated by NVD at review time.
- Description: NVD received a new Linux kernel CVE from kernel.org on July 4, 2026, describing an IPv6 paged-allocation path issue where fraggap handling can undersize a buffer and lead to a write past the end of the socket buffer area.
- Why it needs review: Ubuntu is in Products.txt and Ubuntu ships Linux kernel packages, but the source found in this window is the upstream kernel/NVD record. I did not find a matching Ubuntu Security Notice confirming affected Ubuntu releases during this run, so this should not yet be treated as a confirmed Ubuntu finding.
- Source: NVD CVE-2026-53362 (https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-53362).

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for managed Edge deployments because the July 3 Edge batch includes remote-code-execution-class browser issues and at least one Critical-severity CVE entry. For Ubuntu/Linux kernel, monitor for an Ubuntu Security Notice or package status update before treating CVE-2026-53362 as confirmed exposure. No other monitored product had a confirmed fresh finding in this run.
